title: Sales agent: semantic model for Dynamics 365 and Salesforce CRM data
summary: Hold the briefing because its glossary control reports automation as undocumented even though the cited Dataverse reference provides glossary-term operations. The rollout qualifications, licensing and portal destinations are supported; a descriptive detail about form display names and minor navigation issues also need correction.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans a semantic model to help Sales agent understand CRM structure and meaning.
claims.quote: Semantic model helps Sales Agent understand the structure and meaning of an organization’s CRM data.

claims.claim: The planned representation includes tables or objects, fields, descriptions, data types, relationships, views, pick-list values and glossary terms.
claims.quote: It creates a connected representation of CRM metadata, including tables or objects, fields, descriptions, data types, relationships, views, pick-list values, and glossary terms.

claims.claim: The roadmap says retrieving this context should improve interpretation of business language and questions spanning related CRM records.
claims.quote: Sales Agent can retrieve this context when responding to questions, improving its ability to interpret business language and answer complex questions that span related CRM records.

claims.claim: The roadmap places Dynamics 365 semantic-model enablement in Power Apps Maker Portal.
claims.quote: Dynamics 365 admins can enable and turn on semantic model in Power Apps Maker Portal

claims.claim: The roadmap says Dynamics 365 administrators can configure the model's data coverage and signals.
claims.quote: configure the data coverage and signals that Sales Agent should use. Admins can configure the underlying data, views, metadata and relationships used in the model.

claims.claim: For Salesforce, the roadmap says the model will be based on existing Sales agent table and glossary configuration.
claims.quote: For Salesforce customers, the semantic model will be based on existing Sales agent table and glossary configuration in Sales agent settings or Power Apps Maker Portal.

claims.claim: The roadmap says Salesforce administrators can configure additional relationship and view signals in Power Apps Maker Portal.
claims.quote: In Power Apps Maker Portal, Salesforce admins will can configure additional Salesforce signals to use in semantic model such as relationships and views.

claims.claim: Learn defines signal-type, table and individual-item control levels within a semantic model.
claims.quote:
Signal-type level | Enable or disable a signal type across all tables in the selected model.
Table level | Add or remove a table from the selected model, or change which signals it contributes.
Item level | Enable or disable a generated view or relationship within a table.

claims.claim: Administrators can turn semantic-model signal types on or off.
claims.quote:
Open the model and select Configure.
Under Manage signals, turn the relevant signal On or Off.

claims.claim: Administrators can disable individual outdated or misleading views and relationships.
claims.quote: Views and relationships within a table can be individually disabled when they contain outdated, incorrect, or misleading data that negatively affects agent responses.

claims.quote: Changes are picked up during regeneration. To request an earlier run instead of waiting for the scheduled cycle, see Regenerate the semantic model.
